title: Helen Haines: independent MP in critical condition in Melbourne’s Alfred hospital after being struck by car in Wangaratta – follow updates
summary: A joint counter-terrorism taskforce is investigating the incident, which Anthony Albanese alleged ‘wasn’t an accident’

blocks.text: Key events

items: 13m agoHelen Haines still in critical condition: Albanese
16m agoAnthony Albanese: 'This is a tragic situation'

blocks.text: It “beggars belief” that Helen Haines would be involved in an incident like this, Victorian National MP Tim McCurdy told ABC’s RN this mornng.
double quotation markHelen is just a lovely person, and I just cannot for the life of me see how anyone could take offence at Helen and have this attitude towards her. It’s just appalling.

McCurdy says he heard about the incident after the state emergency service called him yesterday to “describe what they could”. McCurdy, whose electorate, takes in Wangaratta where the incident occurred, said he usually feels safe in his local area.

double quotation markI mean, all MPs, but particularly regional MPs, we make ourselves available to everybody wherever at any time. And this is what’s so hard to believe: that if you can’t walk down the street in Wangaratta or any other regional town like this with the fear of this going on, it’s just shocking. It’s just got out of hand.
Tess Ikonomou
Asked if security would be stepped up following the attack, Albanese said he doesn’t want policians to lose the ability to engage with their communites.

double quotation markWe take the advice of the security agencies, including, of course, the Australian Federal Police, you know, and we act upon that advice, but I never want to lose the opportunity for people to mix with their representatives. That’s a really important part of our democracy. But we continue to take advice.
He added: “I think we can have disagreements without questioning people’s motives or their patriotism.”
Anthony Albanese says Australians need to turn down the temperature of political and public debate.

double quotation markAll of us are responsible for that. Whether we’re politicians, whether we’re the media, whether we’re citizens, in just being able to discuss things in a civil way. We can have disagreements in a democracy.
Helen Haines still in critical condition: Albanese
Tom McIlroy
Anthony Albanese says the Indi MP, Helen Haines, is still in a critical condition on Tuesday morning, after undergoing surgery last night.
He says Monday’s attack was a deliberate attempt to harm the independent MP.
Albanese has told Seven that he spoke with Haines’ husband, Phil, last night, in the hours after the attack.
A man remains in police custody.
Anthony Albanese: 'This is a tragic situation'
The prime minister is speaking on Channel Seven’s Sunrise program this morning.
He says he will be briefed by police on the investigation into the alleged attack on Helen Haines later this morning, alongside the Victorian premier, Ben Carroll.
double quotation markAt this stage its not clear what that motivation was.

But he alleged: “It is clear that this wasn’t just an accident – this was an attempt to harm Helen Haines outside Wangaratta at her electorate office. Helen was getting things from the boot of her car when this incident occurred.”
He said:
double quotation markThis is a tragic situation. Our thoughts are with her this morning and today and we hope for a full recovery.
What we know so far
First of all let’s set out what we know so far about what happened in Wangaratta yesterday.

items: Helen Haines has been critically injured in an alleged attack involving a car outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, regional Victoria, at about 3.35pm on Monday.
The independent MP was taken to Melbourne’s Alfred hospital and underwent surgery overnight. She remains in a critical condition.

A 43-year-old man from Tarrawingee is in custody, and the alleged attack is being investigated by the Australian federal police, Asio and the joint counter-terror taskforce. The motive is not yet known. A knife was allegedly found in his car after he was detained by a passerby when he got out of his vehicle.

Anthony Albanese, Angus Taylor, the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, the One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, and politicians across the parliament have sent their thoughts and well wishes to Haines and her family.
In a press conference on Monday evening, Albanese described Haines, who has represented Indi since 2019, as a “thoroughly decent human being, full of integrity and respected right across parliament”.

Addressing the media in Wangaratta on Monday evening, acting supt Ashley Mason said police were still investigating whether the incident was targeted. He said there was no ongoing threat to the community and nothing to indicate the parties were known to each other.

Welcome

Good morning and welcome to our rolling coverage of the alleged attack on the independent MP for Indi, Helen Haines. She is in a critical condition in Melbourne’s Alfred hospital after being struck by a car ourtside her electorate office in Wangaratta yesterday afternoon. A 43-year-old local man is in custody over the incident.
We will have the latest developments and reaction.
